name: Signs You've Outgrown Your Setup
why_it_works: A self-diagnosis checklist makes the viewer count along. Each sign they recognize raises the score in their head, and by the end they have talked themselves into needing an upgrade. Nobody likes being sold to, but everyone likes scoring themselves.

hook.pattern: Ask the viewer to keep score of how many signs apply to them.
examples: Count how many of these apply to you.
Four signs you've outgrown your {{current_setup}}. Three means it's time.
If number three made you wince, we need to talk.

variables.name: sign_1
variables.example: you re-record vocals because of the neighbor's dog

variables.name: sign_2
variables.example: your mixes sound different in the car every time

variables.name: sign_3
variables.example: you turned down a feature because you couldn't deliver stems

variables.name: sign_4
variables.example: you're already planning the next project before this one is out

variables.name: upgrade
variables.description: What the brand offers as the next step
variables.example: a day of studio time with an engineer

beats.on_screen_text: Count how many apply to you.
beats.voiceover: Count how many of these apply to you.

visual.prompt: A cramped home version of a {{current_setup}}, cluttered corner, single desk lamp, slightly frustrating mood, vertical 9:16
Close-up of a person's tired face lit by a screen late at night, shallow depth of field, cool light, vertical
A phone on a desk showing an unanswered message notification, the room dark around it, single light source, vertical
A notebook full of plans and sketches open on a desk, morning light coming in, hopeful mood, vertical

beats.voiceover: Three or more? You're ready for {{upgrade}} at {{brand}}.

visual.prompt: Slow reveal walk-through of a polished {{brand}} space, warm practical lights coming on one by one, wide to medium, vertical 9:16

cta: Scored three or more? Start with a {{offer}}.

craft.notes: Giving a threshold (three or more) before the list starts turns passive watching into counting. Order the signs mild, mild, painful, aspirational: the painful one creates the need and the aspirational one leaves the viewer feeling capable, not ashamed, right before the offer.

do_not: Shame the viewer's current situation; signs should feel familiar, not insulting
Use signs that apply to everyone; the list loses meaning
compliance: Real estate: no promises about home values, sale prices or timelines; include brokerage name and license info per state rules
Insurance: no guarantees of coverage or savings; signs describe situations, not policy advice; include license info where required
